name: Launch the Portal
description: Stand up a company's logged-in FluidOS portal in one run: resolve the portal app, build the chosen pages in parallel from working component trees, reconcile navigation, publish a version, and verify the published state against the API. The Day-1 counterpart to speed-import — that one builds the storefront, this one builds the portal behind the login. Expects a caller `context` with definition_id, navigation_id, pages, page_positions, and optionally company_id, portal_url and audience.

steps.name: Resolve the portal app and inventory it
steps.prompt:
Establish — and prove — the portal app every later step writes into. Do not create any screens here.

1. Read `context.definition_id` and `context.navigation_id` from the `## Context from caller` block. When `definition_id` is the string `NEW`, create a definition first (`POST {{company.api_base}}/api/company/fluid_os/definitions` with `{ "definition": { "name": "<company name> Portal" } }`) and use the id it returns.
2. `GET {{company.api_base}}/api/company/fluid_os/definitions` and confirm the id resolves to a real definition. Record its `name` and `active` flag.
3. `GET {{company.api_base}}/api/company/fluid_os/definitions/<DEF_ID>/screens` — the CURRENT screens. Record every existing `id`, `name` and `slug`.
   **Flag slug collisions explicitly.** A definition often already carries a screen on `home` — the slug the partner/customer home pages want. For every page in `context.pages` whose target slug already exists, say so in STEP_OUTPUT and state how `context.on_slug_collision` resolves it: `update` means the builder edits that existing screen in place; `alongside` means it must pick a non-colliding slug (`home-partner`, `home-customer`) and leave the existing screen untouched. Never silently overwrite a screen this run did not create.
4. Resolve the navigation. `GET .../definitions/<DEF_ID>/navigations` and handle what you actually find — do not assume exactly one:
   - **Exactly one** — use it.
   - **Several** — a definition commonly carries both a `Main Navigation` and a `Mobile Navigation`. The MAIN one is the target; record the others by id and name so the reconcile step knows to leave them alone. `context.navigation_id` wins when the caller supplied it.
   - **None** — a brand-new definition can have zero navigations. Try `POST .../definitions/<DEF_ID>/navigations` with `{ "navigation": { "name": "Main Navigation" } }` and re-`GET` to confirm. If that shape is rejected, do NOT guess variants: end with `STEP_OUTPUT: BLOCKED — definition <id> has no navigation and POST .../navigations was rejected (<exact error>); a navigation must exist before pages can be linked.`
   Record the chosen navigation id and every existing item (`id`, `label`, `slug`, `position`).
5. Inventory the content the page builders will need, so five parallel steps don't each re-discover it:
   - `GET {{company.api_base}}/api/company/media?per_page=200` — real media (id + URL) to replace `picsum.photos` placeholders.
   - `GET {{company.api_base}}/api/company/v1/products` — real products (id, title, price, URL) to replace `REPLACE_PRODUCT_*` placeholders.
   - `GET {{company.api_base}}/api/droplet_installations` — installed droplets and their `droplet_uuid`s. The page templates embed droplet nodes whose UUIDs belong to the company they were exported from; each builder must remap or delete those nodes.

End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` carrying, as compact JSON the parallel builders can read directly: `definition_id`, `definition_name`, `navigation_id`, `existing_screens` (id/name/slug), `existing_nav_items` (id/label/slug/position), `company_id`, a `media` sample (up to 30 id+url), a `products` sample (up to 30 id/title/price/url), and `installed_droplets` (uuid + name). If any inventory call fails, say so explicitly rather than reporting an empty list as if it were empty upstream.
acceptance: The definition id used is confirmed to exist by a GET against /api/company/fluid_os/definitions, and STEP_OUTPUT names it.
STEP_OUTPUT lists the definition's CURRENT screens (id, name, slug) — an empty list is acceptable only if the GET actually returned none.
Any collision between an existing screen slug and a requested page is flagged, with the on_slug_collision resolution stated.

A navigation id is resolved and its existing items reported. If the definition had none, the step either created one and verified it by re-GET, or reported BLOCKED — it did not proceed as though a navigation existed.
When several navigations exist, the chosen one is named and the others are listed as out of scope.
Media, product and droplet-installation inventories were each fetched; any call that failed is reported as failed rather than as an empty result.
No screen was created, updated or deleted by this step.

steps.name: Build the partner home page
acceptance: A screen exists on the resolved definition whose component_tree is the template's full array — verified by GET .../screens/<id>, not by assertion.
Every top-level section sits inside the single page-wrapper LayoutWidget; no section was lifted out of it.
No `picsum.photos` URL, no `REPLACE_*` token and no `YOUR_COMPANY_ID` remains anywhere in the saved tree.
Droplet nodes were either remapped to a droplet_uuid this company actually has installed, or deleted outright — no foreign UUID survives.
A navigation item points at the screen and carries a non-empty slug.
Any widget lacking real data uses an honest empty state; no fabricated earnings, ranks or counts.

steps.name: Reconcile the portal navigation
steps.prompt:
The page builders ran in parallel and each added its own navigation item, so positions can collide and a rerun can leave duplicates. Reconcile the navigation into one clean, intentional menu.

1. `GET {{company.api_base}}/api/company/fluid_os/definitions/<DEF_ID>/navigations` and the items on the navigation resolved by `resolve-app`. Work ONLY on that navigation — if the definition also carries a `Mobile Navigation` or any other, leave it exactly as it is and say which you skipped. Silently rewriting a second menu is a worse failure than leaving one unsynced.
2. **Delete duplicates.** Two items pointing at the same `screen_id`, or sharing a slug, are a collision — keep the one with the better label and `DELETE .../navigation_items/<id>` the rest.
3. **Every item needs a non-empty `slug`.** An item without one renders as a non-clickable ALL-CAPS section header instead of a link. This is the single most common way a portal page ships invisible — check every item, not just the ones you created.
4. **Assign deliberate positions.** Use `context.page_positions` when the caller supplied it; otherwise order by audience — the everyday home first, then the dashboard, then affiliate/share tools, then any alternate layout last. Positions must be unique and contiguous starting at 1. `PUT .../navigation_items/<id>` to set each.
5. **Every built screen is reachable.** Cross-check the screens created by this run against the final item list; a screen with no navigation item is invisible to users. Add the missing item rather than reporting it as a limitation.

End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` listing the final navigation as an ordered table of position, label, slug and screen_id, plus a line for every duplicate you deleted.
acceptance: A GET of the navigation shows no two items sharing a screen_id or a slug.
Every navigation item has a non-empty slug.
Positions are unique and contiguous starting at 1.
Every screen created by this run has exactly one navigation item pointing at it.
Navigations other than the one resolved by resolve-app were left untouched, and the step names which were skipped.
STEP_OUTPUT reports the final ordered navigation and names every item deleted.

steps.name: Publish a portal version
steps.prompt:
Publish the definition so the work becomes visible to real users.

1. `POST {{company.api_base}}/api/company/fluid_os/definitions/<DEF_ID>/versions` with an empty body `{}`. There is NO `/publish` endpoint — it 404s. Do not go looking for one.
2. Re-`GET .../definitions` and confirm the definition no longer reports `has_pending_changes: true`. If it still does, the publish did not take — report that plainly instead of assuming success.
3. Note the version the POST returned so the QA step and the operator can refer to it.

End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` naming the definition id, the created version, and the post-publish `has_pending_changes` value read back from the API.
acceptance: A POST to .../definitions/<DEF_ID>/versions with an empty body succeeded and the created version is named in STEP_OUTPUT.
The definition was re-read after publishing and its has_pending_changes value is reported from that read, not assumed.
If has_pending_changes is still true, the step says so explicitly rather than claiming a successful publish.

steps.name: Verify the published portal
steps.prompt:
Independently verify the PUBLISHED portal against the live API. You are checking the state a real user would load, not the summaries earlier steps wrote about themselves. Read only — do not fix anything here; report what is wrong and let rework handle it.

For the definition this run targeted:

1. `GET .../definitions/<DEF_ID>/screens` — for EVERY screen this run created, fetch it individually and check the saved `component_tree`:
   - it is the array form, not an empty hash left over from the shell POST;
   - the whole tree sits inside one page-wrapper LayoutWidget;
   - a full-text scan of the serialized tree finds no `picsum.photos`, no `REPLACE_`, no `YOUR_COMPANY_ID`;
   - every `droplet.` node's UUID segment appears in this company's `GET /api/droplet_installations`.
2. `GET` the navigation — every item has a slug, positions are unique and contiguous, and every created screen has exactly one item.
3. `GET .../definitions` — the definition exists and `has_pending_changes` is false.
4. Count what actually shipped versus `context.pages`. A page that was requested and is missing is a FAIL, not a note.

End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` as a per-page table — page, screen id, slug, nav position, placeholders found (should be zero), unresolved droplet nodes (should be zero) — followed by an explicit `PORTAL READY` or `PORTAL NOT READY — <reasons>`.
acceptance: Every screen created by this run was fetched individually and its saved component_tree inspected — not inferred from an earlier step's summary.
A full-text scan of each saved tree finds zero `picsum.photos`, `REPLACE_` and `YOUR_COMPANY_ID` occurrences, and any hit is reported per page.
Every `droplet.` node UUID in every saved tree is confirmed against GET /api/droplet_installations for this company.
The navigation was re-read: every item has a slug, positions are unique and contiguous, and every created screen has exactly one item.
The definition reports has_pending_changes false after publish.
Every page named in context.pages has a corresponding screen; any missing page is reported as a failure.
STEP_OUTPUT ends with an explicit PORTAL READY or PORTAL NOT READY verdict listing the reasons.

steps.name: Hand off to the operator
steps.prompt:
Write the operator's handoff. Short, honest, and useful to someone who did not watch the run.

Cover:
1. **What shipped** — each page, its slug, its navigation position, and the portal-builder link `https://admin.fluid.app/portal-builder/<DEF_ID>`.
2. **What to look at first** — the pages carrying the most placeholder-swapped content, since those are where a wrong product or image will show.
3. **What is still generic** — every place you used an honest empty state or generic copy because the company had no real data. Name them; this is the operator's to-do list, and it is the most valuable part of this handoff.
4. **What needs a human decision** — anything a page implies the business must choose (which products to feature, whether the alternate home replaces the primary, which droplets to install).
5. **Anything QA flagged** that was accepted rather than fixed.

Do not pad it. If the run was clean, say so in two lines and list the to-dos.
acceptance: Every page that shipped is listed with its slug and navigation position.
The portal-builder link includes the real definition id.
Placeholder/empty-state content left for the operator is named specifically, not summarized as 'some content'.
Any QA finding that was accepted rather than fixed is surfaced.
